correctness.rationale: The neighbor count on L(K_n) yields the precise degree-sum inequalities; these characterize threshold graphs with a no-(n-1)-degree-sum gap. Canonical creation words encode all types uniquely. Zero-to-one turn constraints reduce sparse configurations to endpoint-height-2 paths; explicit two-child inversion gives 2^{k-1}; odd middle types are impossible by the first two zero-vertices; complement maps k to n-1-k. The labelled polynomial follows from degree-class automorphism stabilizers. Separate direct majority exhaustive test n=3..7 and independent creation-word and recursion tests through n=15 passed. Experiments are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact unlabeled (under original ground-set permutations) fixed-point classification for the natural triangular-graph family and exposes a missing middle creation-word class. The 2^{floor(n/2)} count comes from a nontrivial path bijection, not a routine substitution in a general labelled fixed-point formula. An exact labelled occupation polynomial and transparent boundary exclude 2-cycles; the result is motivated by identifying stable states and their symmetry types on a canonical highly connected graph.
